To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

two E-selectin ligand glycoproteins, BST-2, and LGALS3, are associated with poor prognosis in breast cancer, and that their combined expression is predictive of liver and brain relapse in ER-negative tumours.

1) BST-2 and sLex are both independent prognostic markers of distant metastasis and poor prognosis in breast cancer; 2) the combination of BST-2 and the sLex carbohydrate defines a subgroup of patients with ERnegative tumours at higher risk of liver and brain relapse; 3) BST-2 is a new prognostic marker of poor prognosis in breast carcinoma.
the expression of two E-selectin ligand proteins, BST-2 or LGALS3BP together with sLex, is associated with poor outcome in ER-negative breast cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new biomarkers for breast cancer prognosis.
the identification of novel markers that could improve the stratification of ER-negative breast cancers and help to identify patients who could be considered for more aggressive treatment strategies.
the identification of new prognostic markers for ER-negative breast cancer and with the characterisation of their role in metastasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of sLex with the molecular scaffold is crucial in order to define the metastatic potential of breast cancer cells.

the presence of BST2 and sLex together is a poor prognostic marker in patients with ER-negative breast cancer and that these markers could potentially be used as a tool in clinical practice for risk assessment and treatment decision-making.

high expression of sLex in combination with high expression of BST2 is associated with poor survival in ER-negative breast cancer patients, and this association may be stronger than the association of sLex alone with poor survival.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of sLex with the two glycoproteens (BST-2, LGALS3BP) is a better predictor of metastasis and survival than sLex alone in patients with ER-negative breast cancer.
the combination of two selectin ligands, sLex and BST-2, may help to identify a subgroup of ER-negative tumours at higher risk of metastatic progression and poorer survival.
the combination of sLex expression with its carriers (e.g. BST-2) is a more accurate predictor of metastasis and poorer survival in breast cancer than each marker independently.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of selectin ligands with their carriers can provide more relevant information than each marker independently.
the combination of sLex with its carriers may be more relevant than sLex expression alone for predicting the metastatic behaviour of breast tumours.
sLex expression in combination with its carriers may be more informative than each marker alone.
